Looking at the z-index values for each box:
- `root>back`: z-index: 1
- `root>middle`: z-index: 3
- `root>front`: z-index: 2

In CSS stacking, higher z-index values render on top of lower ones. Even though the node is named "front", the actual stacking order is determined by the z-index values, not the names. The point (120, 120) falls within all three boxes, but the one with the highest z-index will be visible.

ANSWER: root>middle
